one_line: A sticky-note board where a browser agent collaborates visibly with the user.
what_it_does: Lets humans and an agent read, split, claim, move, and comment on notes across boards with shared visible state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent typed access to shared board state and visible claims/provenance in the user's session; UI-driving automation would be materially less reliable for multi-step edits.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 13 tools for reading boards, creating/moving notes, switching boards, claiming notes, and commenting.
Packet says claim pills and agent-written badges make concurrent work visible.
execution_rationale: The packaging and described workflow are coherent and the Devpost screenshot shows a real submission with an embedded demo, but the provided packet has no transcript and the referenced frame-sheet evidence was not legible enough to establish end-to-end completion.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows Pinnwall submission packaging and an embedded project video.
Packet describes a concrete split-one-note-into-four workflow and shared-state affordances.
impact_rationale: A clear audience of people using lightweight boards gains practical value from delegating repetitive board maintenance while retaining visibility and control.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies sticky-note users and a concrete multi-task note workflow.
Agent actions and responses remain visible on the board.
creativity_rationale: The teammate framing, claims, comments, and provenance badges are a fresh synthesis for a familiar board category.
creativity_evidence: Shared human-agent board state is central to the concept.
Claim pills and agent-written badges make collaboration legible.
usability_note: The board metaphor and visible ownership cues should be easy to understand; no direct observed usability test is supplied.
red_flags: No transcript and limited direct execution evidence in the packet.
standouts: No separate credential or server-auth burden claimed.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-centered collaboration concept with credible practical value.

one_line: A WebMCP-native marketplace where outside agents and people organize evidence on a shared canvas.
what_it_does: Supports discovery, comparison, boards, cited research, acquisition-cost calculations, offers, and human approval gates for commerce workflows.
leverage_rationale: The persistent shared canvas and structured marketplace state let an outside agent investigate and organize alongside the human in ways that ordinary UI driving would not replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes durable sessions, focused tool packs, shared boards, cited notebooks, comparisons, and structured trade rooms.
Transcript explicitly shows human-only approval at publishing, contacting, offering, and trade-advancement boundaries.
execution_rationale: The long video transcript and frame sheets describe and visibly support a broad, coherent marketplace workflow, though the breadth leaves some end-to-end claims unverified.
execution_evidence: Video transcript walks through signed-out setup, sign-in rediscovery, catalog browsing, agent panels, and approval boundaries.
Frames visibly show catalog cards, filters, agent launcher/panels, and a boat detail view.
impact_rationale: Collectors and buyers of complex used goods have a real research and decision-making problem, and the shared evidence workspace addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Packet names cars, boats, campers, motorcycles, and machinery buyers as the audience.
Transcript describes research notebooks, comparable sales, risks, budgets, and trade scenarios.
creativity_rationale: The outside-agent marketplace, persistent canvas, focused capability activation, and explicit verification boundary form a notably ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Product contains no embedded LLM and instead collaborates with agents users already trust.
Shared canvas persists findings, decisions, alerts, offers, and multi-party trade state.
usability_note: Canvas-first organization and explicit approvals are promising, though the large scope may create complexity.
red_flags: Very broad claimed scope relative to hackathon evidence.
standouts: Human control is designed into consequential transitions.
advance_reason: Most compelling combination of WebMCP leverage, ambitious concept, and visible product workflow.

one_line: A local-first registry and runtime that turns reviewed action packs into WebMCP tools in a signed-in tab.
what_it_does: Binds declarative, origin-specific packs to live sessions with drift checks, bounded outputs, and human approval for consequential writes.
leverage_rationale: The product directly addresses the missing agent surface for existing authenticated sites; its runtime makes typed, narrow, inspectable interaction possible without vendor APIs or separate credentials.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes origin/fingerprint binding, declarative manifests, bounded output projection, and live tools in the user's session.
Research measured 429 likely tool locations across three products and zero registrations, motivating the runtime.
execution_rationale: The architecture is unusually coherent and packaging includes six gallery images, but there is no submitted video and the packet does not demonstrate a complete live pack execution.
execution_evidence: Devpost facts report a live demo, public repo, and six gallery images.
Description specifies concrete safety and drift-fail-closed mechanisms.
impact_rationale: If reliable, this can unlock agent assistance across the large class of authenticated operational sites that lack APIs, with a credible safety model for adoption.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies Grafana, Cal.com, payer portals, vendor consoles, and admin dashboards as target environments.
Runtime preserves existing session permissions and restricts packs by origin and reviewed fingerprint.
creativity_rationale: Inverting API adoption from vendor-side implementation to user-installed reviewed action packs is a highly original and ambitious infrastructure idea.
creativity_evidence: Login-as-API reframe is central to the design.
Declarative-only packs and bounded untrusted output address distinct agent safety problems.
usability_note: Pack review, origin binding, and drift handling could be powerful but likely impose meaningful setup and comprehension costs.
red_flags: No video; central runtime behavior is claimed rather than directly demonstrated.
Broad generality may exceed the evidence.
standouts: Safety boundaries are concrete rather than purely aspirational.
advance_reason: High-impact, highly differentiated agent-infrastructure concept; execution evidence is the main uncertainty.

one_line: An analyst-first SOC workbench where agents investigate bounded evidence and humans approve consequences.
what_it_does: Runs approved investigation skills, exposes KQL and raw records, builds an evidence graph, and stages responses while reserving sufficiency and closure decisions for analysts.
leverage_rationale: Structured case-bound tools, fixed KQL contracts, revision binding, and live evidence graphs make agent investigation more precise and auditable than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies case/revision-bound tools and fixed KQL contracts.
Agent actions add evidence to a live graph while response approval remains human-controlled.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and the packet provides a coherent architecture, synthetic-data boundary, and four gallery images; lack of video limits end-to-end certainty.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo and four gallery images.
Description covers investigation, impact modeling, response staging, and closure boundaries.
impact_rationale: Security analysts have a concrete need for faster investigation without losing evidence provenance or authority over response actions.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies escalated cases and exact KQL/raw-record review as the target workflow.
Synthetic data and non-contacting response actions appropriately bound the demo.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-first graph and explicit human authority boundary are a thoughtful, domain-specific interaction model rather than a generic chatbot wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Exact query and raw-record visibility are part of the interaction.
Evidence sufficiency and restricted telemetry gates are retained by the analyst.
usability_note: Analyst-oriented evidence visibility is promising; graph readability is acknowledged as a design challenge.
red_flags: Synthetic data only; no direct production integration demonstrated.
standouts: Evidence remains inspectable rather than reduced to a summary.
advance_reason: Focused, credible SOC workflow with meaningful structured-agent value.

one_line: A stable preview and review session where an agent can act on precisely anchored visual feedback.
what_it_does: Captures DOM context, selector, viewport, and version from reviewer gestures, then lets an agent inspect styles, focus elements, reply, and preserve comments across redeploys.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP places the agent in the same live review context, exposing structured anchors and viewport controls that eliminate manual translation from screenshots and prose.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says the page publishes 13 tools for structured review reading, exact comment focus, viewport switching, CSS inspection, and thread replies.
Stable URL preserves comments and version context across publishes.
execution_rationale: The 149-second video transcript gives a specific end-to-end review-to-fix sequence and frames visibly show the product; some later coding-agent behavior remains described rather than fully evidenced.
execution_evidence: Video transcript describes click capture, 390px reproduction, CSS inspection, reply, redeploy, and resolution.
Devpost packaging shows an embedded project video.
impact_rationale: Design and development teams routinely lose time translating visual feedback into actionable source context; this directly shortens that loop.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies screenshot-plus-sentence feedback and the first ten minutes of translation as the problem.
Stable review URLs and anchored comments preserve context for reviewers and developers.
creativity_rationale: The same-tab review-session concept and viewport/style-aware agent collaboration are a fresh, well-pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Reviewer gesture becomes structured, versioned context rather than an out-of-band screenshot.
Agent can bring the reviewer back to the exact referenced element.
usability_note: The direct click-to-comment workflow and stable URL are highly legible and reduce coordination friction.
red_flags: Some claims about source fixing depend on an external coding agent not directly shown in the supplied evidence.
standouts: Excellent alignment between WebMCP and the core problem.
advance_reason: Clear, focused, and demonstrably useful WebMCP workflow.

one_line: A cloud-incident command center where an agent maps blast radius and stages human-approved remediation.
what_it_does: Uses a Kanban-style operational board for critical incidents, workload routing, bounty prioritization, and mock IaC patch staging.
leverage_rationale: Structured JSON-schema state mutations can make multi-column incident orchestration more reliable, but the packet does not establish that generic automation could not achieve similar results.
leverage_evidence: Description says WebMCP exposes strict JSON-schema React state mutations.
Human engineers retain click approval for staged configurations.
execution_rationale: The concept and one gallery image suggest a prototype command center, but no frame sheets, public repo, or end-to-end execution evidence are supplied.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo and one gallery image.
About text describes three board columns and staged patches but is truncated before full workflow detail.
impact_rationale: Infrastructure incident response is a high-value audience and the proposed blast-radius and workload coordination address real operational pain, albeit with mock remediation.
impact_evidence: Packet names GKE, Cloud SQL, Slack, and Jira incident-management pain points.
Staged remediation preserves human approval.
creativity_rationale: Combining incident orchestration, workload-burnout routing, and an incentivized priority exchange is an ambitious hackathon synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Three-column command-center model includes a bounty/priority exchange.
Agent stages Terraform/Bash-like patches rather than executing them directly.
usability_note: The operational board is understandable, but multiple concepts and approval flows may be cognitively heavy.
red_flags: No public repository and only one gallery image.
Core workflow is largely claimed in text.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable, but evidence is too thin to rank above better-demonstrated projects.

one_line: A conversational assistant that fills a visible Indonesian individual tax-return draft while the user reviews it.
what_it_does: Translates plain-language life and income facts into section-level form updates, leaving review and submission under user control.
leverage_rationale: Section-level typed tools can translate natural language into precise tax fields while preserving the visible form, reducing classification and navigation errors compared with UI clicking.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes conversational extraction of salary, deductions, and family status into visible form sections.
Human review and submission control are central to the workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a plausible focused workflow and reports a live demo, but there is no video and the visible evidence is packaging/gallery-oriented rather than end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Facts report public repo and live demo.
About text describes the problem, section-level tools, and visible-draft workflow.
impact_rationale: The target audience is large and the problem—mapping ordinary personal descriptions to complex Indonesian tax classifications—is concrete and consequential.
impact_evidence: Packet cites 13 million returns and widespread procedural confusion.
Solution directly addresses classification and form-navigation burden while retaining review.
creativity_rationale: Conversational tax preparation is a known pattern, but visible section-level WebMCP collaboration and user-controlled submission provide a meaningful domain-specific angle.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language interview is mapped to detailed government form categories.
Assistant operates alongside the visible form rather than hiding form logic.
usability_note: Conversation can lower the learning curve, but tax corrections and edge cases demand careful feedback.
red_flags: No video evidence; tax correctness is not independently demonstrated.
About text includes externally attributed statistics that are not verified in this packet.
standouts: Visible draft plus human submission gate is appropriate for high-stakes forms.
advance_reason: High-impact use case with meaningful WebMCP leverage despite moderate execution evidence.

one_line: A persistent shared workspace where humans and multiple agents maintain project state across conversations.
what_it_does: Stores tasks, knowledge, decisions, activity, proposals, and context as structured state with resident-agent interpretation and human authorization.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects multiple external agents to durable shared workspace state, addressing cross-conversation continuity that ordinary single-chat UI automation handles poorly.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes external agents discovering workspaces and inspecting structured context.
Tasks, decisions, knowledge, and activity persist independently of any conversation.
execution_rationale: Five gallery images and a coherent description indicate a substantial interface, but no video, public repo, or demonstrated end-to-end agent operation is supplied.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo and five gallery images.
Description names workspace overview, activity, decisions, import preview, and task execution surfaces.
impact_rationale: Long-running projects and teams have a real need for a source of truth that survives agent and conversation changes.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies isolated conversations as the problem.
Persistent tasks, decisions, and project context directly address continuity.
creativity_rationale: Persistent multi-agent shared state is a strong synthesis, though workspace and knowledge-base products are established categories.
creativity_evidence: Resident Agent interprets changes and highlights conflicts/gaps.
Specialist import agent turns a repository into a structured workspace.
usability_note: The workspace metaphor is familiar; multi-agent activity and authority controls could add complexity.
red_flags: Agent behavior and persistence are described more than directly demonstrated.
standouts: Multi-agent continuity is a credible need.
advance_reason: Good concept, but evidence is too thin for advancement over demonstrated workflows.

one_line: A map-first prospecting platform that turns weak local-business web presence into actionable agency leads.
what_it_does: Discovers and enriches local businesses, analyzes opportunities, generates briefs, selects services, and moves leads through a visual pipeline with agent-synchronized map state.
leverage_rationale: Frontend WebMCP tools synchronize agent actions with map position, focus, zoom, and view state, adding meaningful shared context, though much backend capability already existed via MCP.
leverage_evidence: Packet explicitly distinguishes existing headless MCP backend from new frontend tools.
Tools read map state, move/zoom/frame results, focus businesses, and navigate the interface.
execution_rationale: Ten gallery images and a coherent live-demo packet provide strong evidence of a substantial, consistent prospecting workflow; the core agent invocation is less directly established without video.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo and ten gallery images.
Description covers discovery through delivery and the synchronization challenge.
impact_rationale: Small agencies and developers have a concrete prospecting and qualification workload, and an integrated map-to-project pipeline can save substantial time.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies outdated local-business experiences and agency prospect research as the problem.
Workflow connects discovery, analysis, service selection, outreach, and delivery.
creativity_rationale: The map-first opportunity-to-project pipeline is a useful synthesis; the WebMCP addition is more incremental because backend MCP already existed.
creativity_evidence: Frontend map synchronization is treated as part of agent collaboration.
Pipeline moves from geographic discovery to ready-to-build service opportunities.
usability_note: Map-first discovery and visual pipeline are likely intuitive for agency prospecting, subject to data quality.
red_flags: WebMCP contribution is narrower than the pre-existing backend MCP capability.
standouts: Strong breadth of visible product surfaces.
advance_reason: Well-evidenced, useful product with a meaningful though not transformative WebMCP delta.

one_line: A diabetes log where a person and browser agent share glucose, meal, and insulin context.
what_it_does: Visualizes glucose history, records meals and events with agent provenance, and exposes bounded tools with safety boundaries for assistance.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared health-log state and provenance can reduce repeated context entry and support more precise agent assistance, but the packet does not show that generic automation could not do much of the same.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes a live dashboard, seven-day graph with meal markers, three registered tools, and agent provenance.
Safety boundaries are presented as a product surface.
execution_rationale: Seven gallery images provide substantial packaging and UI evidence for a focused dashboard, but no video or direct end-to-end agent run is included.
execution_evidence: Facts report a live demo and seven gallery images.
Gallery labels include dashboard, graph, tools, meal log, and safety boundaries.
impact_rationale: People with Type 1 diabetes have a real daily tracking and pattern-recognition burden, and a shared log can reduce friction; clinical safety limits remain important.
impact_evidence: Packet grounds the concept in the reviewer's own Type 1 diabetes management experience.
Dashboard combines glucose, meals, and insulin context for pattern exploration.
creativity_rationale: Agent provenance and bounded collaboration inside a diabetes dashboard are a thoughtful domain adaptation, though logging apps and assistants are known categories.
creativity_evidence: Meal entries visibly distinguish agent provenance.
Safety boundaries are made explicit in the interface.
usability_note: A graph-plus-log dashboard can support daily review, but health data entry and interpretation require careful safeguards.
red_flags: No video and no demonstrated clinical validation.
Health recommendations could be high-stakes; packet emphasizes logging rather than diagnosis.
standouts: Agent provenance and safety boundaries are visible concepts.
advance_reason: Credible health-tracking use case with adequate UI evidence and meaningful shared-state potential.
